demonstracao.d: An SFT example: a prompt (system, user, tools, history) and the response the assistant should give. It can be written by humans, generated by a stronger model, or generated by the model itself and then filtered (RFT).

alinhamento-superficial.d: LIMA's proposal: almost all knowledge comes from pretraining, and post-training mostly teaches format and style. With 1,000 curated examples on a LLaMA-65B, the answers were equivalent to or preferred over GPT-4's in 43% of cases.

mascara-de-perda.d: A vector \( m_t \in \{0,1\} \) that decides which positions enter the cross-entropy. In conversational SFT it is 1 on what the assistant writes (including the end of turn) and 0 on the system, the user, and tool results. Implemented with the label −100.

ignore-index.d: A label value that PyTorch's cross-entropy ignores: the position enters neither the sum nor the denominator and produces no gradient. This is how frameworks implement the loss mask.

acumulacao-de-gradientes.d: Summing the gradients of several micro-batches before an optimizer step, to simulate a larger batch. The loss must be normalized by the total number of loss tokens in the accumulated batch; averaging per-micro-batch means gives each token a different weight (the 2024 bug).

kl-direto.d: \( \mathrm{KL}(p\,\|\,q) \) with the reference \( p \) first. It is what SFT's cross-entropy minimizes (\( H(p,q) = H(p) + \mathrm{KL}(p\|q) \)). It is mass-covering: it punishes the model for giving no mass to anything the data does.

kl-reverso.d: \( \mathrm{KL}(q\,\|\,p) \), computed on samples from the model \( q \) itself. It is mode-seeking: it punishes putting mass where the reference puts none, so the model concentrates on the modes it can represent. It is the KL of anchored RL and of on-policy distillation.

neftune.d: An SFT variant that adds uniform noise to the embeddings during training (neftune_noise_alpha in TRL). A hypothesis to measure on your own suite, not a default.

sfttrainer.d: TRL's SFT trainer. It accepts conversations, prompt–completion pairs, tools, and pre-tokenized datasets; it applies the chat template, the mask (assistant_only_loss, completion_only_loss), and packing, and it logs loss, entropy, mean_token_accuracy, and grad_norm.

preserve-thinking.d: A Qwen3.8 chat template kwarg (default true on the card) that keeps the reasoning of previous turns in the history. It must be the same in training and serving; several Qwen3 templates strip the old <think>.

padding-de-sequencia.d: Filling the sequences of a batch with filler tokens up to the length of the longest one. The filler tokens stay out of the loss, but they still cost memory and compute, unless you use packing or padding-free.

best-fit-decreasing.d: A bin-packing heuristic: sorts the examples from largest to smallest and puts each one in the fullest row where it still fits. It is TRL's default packing strategy ("bfd").

padding-free.d: A mode in which the batch becomes a single concatenated sequence, with position_ids restarted per example and variable-length attention (FlashAttention varlen) that keeps one example from attending to another. TRL turns it on with "bfd" packing.

contaminacao-de-lote.d: In a packed batch without a per-example mask, the tokens of one example attend to those of another. The model learns false dependencies between unrelated texts.

descontaminacao.d: Removing from the training data everything that overlaps with the evaluation benchmarks, so that the measured score is not memory. Tülu 3 decontaminated its SFT mix and published what it removed.

destilacao-off-policy.d: Generating responses with a stronger teacher and running SFT on them (sequence-level KD), or minimizing the KL to the teacher's logits on sequences the student did not generate. Alpaca, R1-Distill, and OpenThoughts use the sequence-level version.

star.d: Self-Taught Reasoner (Zelikman et al., 2022): RFT in which, for the questions the model gets wrong, the correct answer is given as a hint and the model writes a justification (rationalization), which also goes into the SFT.

chunked-nll.d: TRL's default SFT loss: it discards the positions with label −100 before the lm_head and computes the cross-entropy in chunks, without materializing the logits tensor \([s \times V]\). It is not compatible with Liger, PEFT, or VLMs.

gkd.d: Generalized Knowledge Distillation (Agarwal et al., ICLR 2024): distillation on the student's own sequences, with a choice of divergence. In TRL it is the DistillationTrainer, with the generalized JSD controlled by beta.

jsd-generalizada.d: \( \beta\,\mathrm{KL}(p_T\|p_M) + (1-\beta)\,\mathrm{KL}(p_S\|p_M) \), with \( p_M = (1-\beta)p_S + \beta p_T \). In TRL, \(\beta = 0\) uses the forward KL and \(\beta = 1\) the reverse KL (the extremes are handled separately).

vantagem-por-token.d: \( \hat A_t = \mathrm{sg}[\log\pi_T(y_t) - \log\pi_\theta(y_t)] \) on the token the student sampled: positive when the teacher likes it more than the student does. It turns on-policy distillation into a policy gradient that fits into PPO/GRPO frameworks.

mopd2.d: Multi-Prefix Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MiMo-V2.6): mixRL and SFT teachers; three streams in the same update — full rollouts, prefixes from teacher trajectories (k turns → k prefixes), and prefixes from SFT demonstrations, from which the student writes one turn.

trl.d: Hugging Face's post-training library (1.14.1 as of 2026-10): SFT, DPO, KTO, reward, RLOO, GRPO, and distillation, with a CLI (trl sft, trl distillation…), Accelerate profiles, and generation with vLLM. PPOTrainer was removed in 1.13.

mlx-lm.d: Training on Apple Silicon: LoRA, DoRA, and full fine-tuning (0.32.0). On a quantized model it automatically becomes QLoRA; scale multiplies \(BA\) directly (it is not PEFT's \(\alpha\)); --mask-prompt trains only the last message.

esquecimento-catastrofico.d: Loss of old capabilities (instruction following, safety, general reasoning, format) when tuning the model for something new. It tracks the KL between the tuned model and the base on the new task's distribution; it is mitigated with replay, a lower LR, LoRA, and on-policy distillation.

rls-razor.d: A result from Shenfeld et al. (2025): forgetting is determined by the distribution shift, measured as the KL between the tuned model and the base on the new task. On-policy RL forgets less than SFT at the same performance because it tends toward minimum-KL solutions.
